mainTopic: Slaughtering a stolen animal in a forbidden way (on שבת, for עבודה זרה, a שור הנסקל), and whether the 'five oxen' fine applies to half-shares owned by partners.
overview: The ברייתא lists cases where a thief's שליח slaughters a stolen animal in a way that cannot make it permitted: on שבת, for עבודה זרה, or a שור הנסקל. רבי מאיר makes the thief pay four or five times, and the רבנן exempt him. The גמרא explains that, by the view that food made on שבת is forbidden only מדרבנן, the רבנן exempt only in the עבודה זרה and שור הנסקל cases. רבא then defends רבי מאיר. In the עבודה זרה case, the worship begins only when the slaughter is finished. In the שור הנסקל case, the ox was with a שומר, and רבי מאיר holds like רבי יעקב and רבי שמעון that דבר הגורם לממון כממון דמי. רב כהנא and רב זביד discuss whether the משנה can follow רבי מאיר and not רבי שמעון. Then רבא asks רב נחמן whether a thief who admitted to one of two partners still owes the fine to the other: does 'five oxen' include five half-oxen? רב נחמן first says no and defends this against challenges from the משנה about a son who stole from his father. The next morning he reverses himself and says half-oxen do count. His explanation for the change continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The שבת case fits only one view of food made on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The view that מעשה שבת is forbidden מן התורה explains why the רבנן exempt in the שבת case. But according to the view that it is only מדרבנן, why would the רבנן exempt?
steps.simpleTranslation: That is why the רבנן exempt him, if food made on שבת is forbidden by Torah law. But according to the one who says it is only a rabbinic ban, why do the רבנן exempt him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its point about the view that food made on שבת is forbidden מן התורה. It then challenges the other view, which says the ban is only מדרבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן exempt because a slaughter that cannot make the meat permitted does not count as a real שחיטה. If the meat of an animal slaughtered on שבת is permitted by Torah law, then that slaughter is a real one. So it is unclear why the רבנן should exempt in the שבת case.

keyTerms.meaning: for this reason
the רבנן exempt (him from paying four or five times)
according to the one who says
a rabbinic ban, not from the Torah
why?

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about whether the thief broke שבת. It is about whether the slaughter counts as a real שחיטה for the payment of four or five times.

phrases.english: for this reason the Rabbis exempt;
but according to the one who says it is rabbinic,
why do the Rabbis exempt?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר דְּרַבָּנַן, אַמַּאי פָּטְרִי רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of the ברייתא across the break.
steps.kashyaTarget: The רבנן's exemption in the שבת case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the meat is permitted by Torah law, the slaughter is a fitting one, so there is no reason to exempt.

steps.title: The Rabbis exempt only in the other two cases
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן's exemption applies only to the cases of עבודה זרה and שור הנסקל, not to the שבת case.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן were referring to the rest of the cases: slaughtering for idol worship and an ox sentenced to stoning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the רבנן never meant to exempt in the שבת case. Their exemption refers only to the other two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the עבודה זרה case and the שור הנסקל case, the meat is forbidden by Torah law, so the slaughter is not fit. In the שבת case the meat is permitted by Torah law according to this view, so even the רבנן agree that the thief pays.

keyTerms.meaning: on the rest (of the cases)
idol worship
an ox sentenced to be stoned, which is forbidden to eat or benefit from

phrases.english: on the rest — on idol worship
phrases.notes: Meaning, the רבנן's exemption was said only about these other cases in the ברייתא.

phrases.english: and an ox that is to be stoned.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the scope of the רבנן's ruling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן exempt in all three cases, including שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבנן exempt only in the עבודה זרה and שור הנסקל cases.
steps.whatToRemember: According to the view that מעשה שבת is only מדרבנן, the רבנן's exemption covers only עבודה זרה and שור הנסקל.

steps.title: Why is רבי מאיר's thief liable in the idol-worship case?
steps.stepSummary: The first bit of slaughter for עבודה זרה already forbids the animal for any benefit. So the rest of the slaughter is done to a forbidden animal that no longer belongs to the owner. Why, then, does רבי מאיר make the thief liable?
steps.simpleTranslation: And as for רבי מאיר, why does he make the thief liable when his agent slaughters for idol worship? As soon as the agent slaughters a little of it, he makes it forbidden. The rest of the slaughter is done on something forbidden for benefit, so he is not slaughtering an animal that belongs to its owner (and not one that belongs to him)!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now challenges רבי מאיר's side of the ברייתא. It asks how he can make the thief liable in the עבודה זרה case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To be liable for paying four or five times, the slaughter must be done to the owner's animal. Slaughter for עבודה זרה forbids the animal as soon as it begins. So most of the slaughter is done to an animal that is אסור בהנאה, has no value, and belongs to no one.

keyTerms.meaning: holds liable
a little bit
he made it forbidden
things forbidden for any benefit
belonging to its owner

steps.confusionAlert: רבי מאיר agrees that an unfit slaughter can still count as a slaughter. The problem here is different: during most of the slaughter, the animal no longer belongs to the owner.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir —
why does he hold liable one who slaughters for idol worship?
once he slaughtered it a little, he made it forbidden;
the rest — it is forbidden for benefit,
and it is not its owner's that he is slaughtering
(and it is not his own that he is slaughtering)!
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר – אַמַּאי מְחַיֵּיב שׁוֹחֵט לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the רבנן's view to a new challenge against רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's ruling that the thief is liable in the עבודה זרה case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The animal becomes אסור בהנאה at the start of the slaughter, so the rest of the slaughter is not done to the owner's animal.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that liability for slaughtering a stolen animal depends on the animal still belonging to the owner during the slaughter.

steps.title: The animal becomes forbidden only at the end of the slaughter
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers the question about עבודה זרה. The case is where the one slaughtering said that only the completion of the slaughter is his act of worship.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This is where he says that he worships the idol only with the completion of the slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question from Step 3. The one slaughtering announced that only the final moment of the slaughter is his act of idol worship.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that the first bit of slaughter should already make the animal forbidden and ownerless. רבא says that here the worship, and so the prohibition, starts only when the slaughter is complete. That is also the moment the thief becomes liable, so throughout the slaughter he is cutting an animal that still belongs to the owner.

keyTerms.meaning: The completion of the slaughter
He worships it (the idol)
In a case where he says (declares his intention)

phrases.english: Rava said:
It is where he says that with the completion of the slaughter
phrases.notes: He declared this before he started slaughtering.

phrases.english: he worships it (the idol).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: בְּאוֹמֵר בִּגְמַר זְבִיחָה הוּא עוֹבְדָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 3 about עבודה זרה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the thief's stated intention delays when the prohibition takes effect.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first bit of slaughter forbids the animal, so the rest is done to an animal that is no longer the owner's.
steps.terutzMaskana: The worship and the prohibition begin only at the completion of the slaughter, so the slaughter is done to the owner's animal.

steps.title: An ox sentenced to stoning belongs to no one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the case of the שור הנסקל. Such an ox is forbidden for benefit, so the thief is slaughtering an animal that is neither the owner's nor his own.
steps.simpleTranslation: An ox that is to be stoned is forbidden for any benefit. He is not slaughtering an animal of its owner, and he is not slaughtering his own animal!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to another case in the ברייתא: a stolen ox that was already sentenced to stoning. It asks how רבי מאיר can make the thief pay four or five times for slaughtering it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once an ox is sentenced to stoning, no one may get any benefit from it, so in money terms it belongs to no one. The fine of four or five times applies when a thief slaughters the owner's animal. Here the ox seems to have no owner at all, so why should the thief pay?

keyTerms.meaning: An ox sentenced to be stoned (because it killed a person)
Things one may not get any benefit from
Belonging to its owner
Slaughters

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about the ox being stolen. It is about whether a forbidden ox still counts as the owner's property at all.

phrases.english: An ox that is to be stoned –
it is something forbidden for any benefit;
it is not its owner's animal that he is slaughtering,
and it is not his own that he is slaughtering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the עבודה זרה case is settled, the same kind of question is asked about the other case, the שור הנסקל.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's ruling that a thief who slaughters a stolen שור הנסקל pays four or five times.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An ox forbidden for benefit has no money value to anyone, so it is not the owner's property. The fine requires slaughtering the owner's animal.

steps.title: The ox was in a guardian's hands, and רבי מאיר holds like רבי יעקב and רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רבא sets the case where the owner gave the ox to a שומר. The ox did damage, was warned, and was sentenced while there. רבי מאיר holds like both רבי יעקב and רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: With what are we dealing here? Where he gave it to a guardian. It did damage in the guardian's house, was warned in the guardian's house, and was sentenced in the guardian's house. And רבי מאיר holds like רבי יעקב, and he holds like רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers by setting the case where the ox was in a guardian's care the whole time and the thief stole it from him. He says רבי מאיר's ruling rests on two other תנאים, which the גמרא will now explain one by one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new detail is the שומר. The ox may be worthless to the owner, but it can still matter money-wise to the guardian, who has to answer to the owner for it. Combining רבי יעקב's view and רבי שמעון's view will show why stealing it causes a real money loss.

keyTerms.meaning: With what are we dealing here? (a formula that narrows the case)
A guardian or bailee holding someone else's item
It was warned (its owners were formally warned about it)
Its verdict was completed (it was sentenced)
He holds like (agrees with) a certain view

phrases.english: Rava said:
With what are we dealing here?
Where the owner handed it over to a guardian;
and it did damage in the guardian's house,
and it was warned in the guardian's house,
and its verdict was completed in the guardian's house.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יַעֲקֹב,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir holds like Rabbi Yaakov,
and he holds like Rabbi Shimon;

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן – כְּגוֹן שֶׁמְּסָרוֹ לְשׁוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 5 by narrowing the case and tying רבי מאיר to two other views.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (הכא במאי עסקינן) plus linking רבי מאיר to other תנאים.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A sentenced ox is worthless and belongs to no one, so slaughtering it should carry no fine.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the ox was with a guardian, and רבי מאיר holds like רבי יעקב and רבי שמעון, stealing it still causes a real money loss.

steps.title: רבי יעקב: a guardian may return a sentenced ox
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the first half of רבא's answer. רבי יעקב holds that even after the ox was sentenced, the guardian can return it to the owner and that counts as returning it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like רבי יעקב, who says: Even after its verdict was completed, if the guardian returned it to the owners, it is considered returned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to unpack רבא's answer, beginning with the רבי יעקב part. רבי יעקב says a guardian clears himself by handing back the sentenced ox, even though it is now worthless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By רבי יעקב's view, the sentenced ox is still useful to the guardian: giving it back frees him from paying the owner. So when the thief steals it, the guardian loses that way of clearing himself. The רבי שמעון part of the answer is explained afterward.

keyTerms.meaning: He returned it
It counts as returned
The owners

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יעקב is not saying the sentenced ox has value to the owner. He is saying the guardian has done his duty once he hands it back.

phrases.english: He holds like Rabbi Yaakov –
who says: Even after its verdict was completed,
if the guardian returned it to the owners –
it is considered returned.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יַעֲקֹב – דְּאָמַר: אַף מִשֶּׁנִּגְמַר דִּינוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first of the two views that רבא named in Step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining one piece of a two-part answer by citing another תנא's rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A worthless, forbidden ox cannot matter money-wise to anyone.
steps.terutzMaskana: By רבי יעקב's view, the guardian can clear himself by returning the sentenced ox, so the ox still matters to him.

steps.title: The second half of רבא's answer: רבי מאיר holds like רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the second part of רבא's answer. רבי מאיר agrees with רבי שמעון that דבר הגורם לממון כממון דמי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר also holds like רבי שמעון, who says: something that causes a money loss is treated like money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains the second half of רבא's answer from step 6. Step 7 explained the רבי יעקב part, and this step explains the רבי שמעון part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sentenced ox itself is worth nothing, because it is forbidden for any benefit. But if the שומר can still return it to the owner (רבי יעקב), then killing it makes the שומר lose money, since he now has to pay for it. Because its loss causes him a money loss, it counts as his money, so the thief is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Something that is not money itself, but whose loss causes a money loss
It is treated like money
And he holds (like this opinion)

steps.confusionAlert: The ox is not worth anything by itself. It only counts as money because of what its loss costs the שומר.

phrases.english: And he holds in accordance with Rabbi Shimon,
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי מאיר. This is the second half of רבא's answer from step 6.

phrases.english: who says: an item that causes money loss
is considered like money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation of רבא's answer. Step 7 explained the רבי יעקב half, and this explains the רבי שמעון half.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings in an outside rule (דבר הגורם לממון) to give a forbidden, worthless animal money value.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A forbidden ox has no value, so the thief took nothing that belongs to anyone.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the שומר loses money when the ox is killed, the ox counts as his money, and the thief is liable.

steps.title: Proof that רבי שמעון holds this rule, from stolen קדשים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה where רבי שמעון makes a thief liable for stolen קדשים that the owner must replace. This shows he holds דבר הגורם לממון כממון דמי.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: רבי שמעון says, with קדשים that the owner is responsible to replace, the thief is liable. So we see that something that causes a money loss is treated like money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that רבי שמעון really holds the rule quoted in step 8, using a משנה about stolen קדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally קדשים are not the owner's money. But if the owner promised to bring a קרבן and must replace the animal if it is lost, then stealing it costs him money. רבי שמעון makes the thief liable, so for him something whose loss causes money loss counts as money.

keyTerms.meaning: Animals set aside for the בית המקדש as קרבנות
He is responsible for them, so he must replace them if they are lost
So we see / this shows
As we learned in a משנה

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna: Rabbi Shimon says:
Sacrificial animals that he is responsible to replace, he is liable;
phrases.notes: The first "he" is the owner who must replace the animal. The second "he" is the thief, who has to pay.

phrases.english: So we see that an item that causes money loss
is considered like money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim in step 8 by showing where רבי שמעון states this rule.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון holds דבר הגורם לממון כממון דמי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה where רבי שמעון makes a thief liable for קדשים that the owner must replace.

steps.title: רב כהנא challenges: the משנה seems to follow רבי שמעון too
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא asked רב זביד: how can we say the משנה follows only רבי מאיר? The משנה says רבי שמעון exempts only in the last two cases, which suggests he agrees with all the rest.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: I repeated this teaching before רב זביד of נהרדעא and asked: can you really explain the משנה as רבי מאיר and not רבי שמעון? The end of the משנה says, רבי שמעון exempts in these two cases. That implies that in the whole rest of the משנה he agrees!
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא challenges the earlier claim that the משנה follows רבי מאיר and not רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה ends by saying רבי שמעון disagrees only on "these two" cases. רב כהנא reads this to mean רבי שמעון agrees with every other case in the משנה. If so, the משנה is not only רבי מאיר's view, but רבי שמעון's too.

keyTerms.meaning: I said this teaching (out loud, before my teacher)
You explain (the source) as following a certain opinion
The last part of the משנה
Exempts, does not make liable
By inference, this implies
Agrees

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said: I said this teaching
before Rav Zevid of Neharde'a, and asked:

phrases.aramaic: מִי מָצֵית מוֹקְמַתְּ מַתְנִיתִין כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר,
phrases.english: Can you really explain the mishna as Rabbi Meir,
and not as Rabbi Shimon?
But it teaches in the last part:
Rabbi Shimon exempts in these two cases;
this implies that in the whole rest of the mishna he agrees!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי מָצֵית מוֹקְמַתְּ מַתְנִיתִין כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר, וְלָא כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from explaining רבי מאיר's view to questioning whether the משנה matches only רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה follows רבי מאיר and not רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since the משנה says רבי שמעון disagrees only on two cases, it implies he agrees with all the other cases. So the משנה fits רבי שמעון too.

steps.title: רב זביד: רבי שמעון agrees only on the case right before
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד answers that the inference is narrower. רבי שמעון only agrees with the case right before, where the thief slaughtered or sold the animal for medicine or for dogs.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד said to him: No. It only implies that רבי שמעון agrees in the case where the thief slaughtered or sold the animal for medicine or for dogs.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד answers רב כהנא's challenge and shrinks the inference to just one nearby case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב כהנא thought "he exempts in these two" means רבי שמעון agrees with everything else in the משנה. רב זביד says it only shows he agrees with the case listed just before them: slaughtering or selling for medicine or dogs. So the rest of the משנה can still follow רבי מאיר and not רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaughtered and sold (the stolen animal)
For medicine
To feed to dogs

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר makes the thief liable for a sentenced ox because he holds like רבי יעקב (the שומר can still return it) and like רבי שמעון (something whose loss costs money counts as money). And "רבי שמעון exempts in these two" only shows he agrees with the case right before them, so the משנה can still follow רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: He said to him: No;
phrases.notes: "He" is רב זביד, answering רב כהנא.

phrases.english: it implies only that he agrees where he slaughtered or sold
for medicine or for dogs.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא; מִכְּלָל דְּמוֹדֵה בְּטָבַח וּמָכַר לִרְפוּאָה וְלִכְלָבִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב כהנא's challenge by limiting what the end of the משנה implies.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the scope of the inference from the משנה's wording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "רבי שמעון exempts in these two" means he agrees with every other case in the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: It only means he agrees with the case right before (medicine or dogs), so the משנה can still follow רבי מאיר and not רבי שמעון.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about stealing from one's father
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line of the משנה about a son who stole from his father, slaughtered or sold the animal, and then the father died.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: If someone stole from his father, then slaughtered or sold the animal, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה to start a new discussion. This line is setting up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the son stole his father's animal and slaughtered or sold it. Afterward the father died, and the son still pays the ארבעה וחמשה fine to the other heirs. This case will soon be used as a challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: He stole from what belongs to his father
He slaughtered or sold it (this triggers the four- or fivefold payment)
And so on (the rest of the quote is left out)

phrases.aramaic: גָּנַב מִשֶּׁל אָבִיו וְטָבַח וּמָכַר וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: He stole from his father's property, and slaughtered or sold it, etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' stands for the rest of the משנה line: afterward his father died, and he still pays four or five times.

steps.triggerLanguage: גָּנַב מִשֶּׁל אָבִיו וְטָבַח וּמָכַר וְכוּ׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section of the גמרא on the next line of the משנה, after the discussion of רבי שמעון ended in Step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A son who steals from his father, slaughters or sells the animal, and then his father dies, still pays the four- or fivefold fine.

steps.title: רבא asks about a thief who admitted to one of two partners
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רב נחמן: if someone stole an ox from two partners, slaughtered it, and admitted to one partner, does he still owe the fine to the other partner? Does 'five oxen' allow 'five half-oxen'?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked רב נחמן: If someone stole an ox that belonged to two partners, slaughtered it, and then admitted the theft to one of them, what is the law? The Torah said 'five oxen'. Does that mean full oxen and not five half-oxen? Or maybe 'five oxen' includes even five half-oxen?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks רב נחמן a question. A thief admitted to one partner, so he is free from that partner's share of the fine. Does he still owe the other partner his half?
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that someone who admits on his own to a קנס (a fine) does not pay it. So the thief is free from one partner's share of the fine. The question is whether the Torah's 'five oxen' only applies when the payment is for whole oxen. If so, a payment of only half-shares would not count, and the thief would owe the second partner no four- or fivefold fine.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him (introduces a question put to a teacher)
Partners, people who own something together
And he admitted
Five oxen, the Torah's fine for stealing and slaughtering or selling an ox
Half-oxen
Or perhaps (introduces the other side of a question)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the thief is completely exempt. He must still return the value of the ox itself. The question is only about the extra fine owed to the partner he did not admit to.

phrases.english: Rava asked Rav Nachman:
If one stole an ox belonging to two partners,
and slaughtered it, and admitted to one of them, what is the law?
phrases.notes: Because he admitted, he is free from that partner's share of the fine. The question is about the other partner.

phrases.english: The Merciful One said 'five oxen',
and not five half-oxen;
or perhaps, the Merciful One said 'five oxen',
and that includes even five half-oxen?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a new question about partners. The case of the משנה just quoted will later be compared to it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the Torah's 'five oxen' fine apply when the thief owes only a half-share, because he admitted to one of two partners?

steps.title: רב נחמן rules that half-oxen do not count
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that the Torah said 'five oxen', not 'five half-oxen', so the thief is exempt from the fine to the second partner.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to him: The Merciful One said 'five oxen', and not five half-oxen.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers רבא's question. The fine applies only to whole oxen, so the thief does not pay the other partner his half of the fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן reads 'five oxen' strictly. Once the thief is exempt from one partner's half, what is left is only a payment of half-oxen. That is not the fine the Torah described, so no fine is paid at all.

keyTerms.meaning: He said to him
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah

phrases.english: He said to him: The Merciful One said 'five oxen',
and not five half-oxen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from Step 13 by choosing the first side.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The thief is exempt from the fine to the second partner, because the Torah's fine is five whole oxen, not five half-oxen.

steps.title: רבא challenges from the son who stole from his father
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects from our משנה. When the father dies, the son inherits part of the animal. That is like admitting to one partner, yet the son still pays the fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא challenged him: The משנה says that if someone stole from his father, slaughtered or sold the animal, and then his father died, he pays four or five times. But here, once his father died, it is like he admitted to one of the partners, and still the משנה teaches that he pays four or five times!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges רב נחמן's answer from the משנה quoted in Step 12. The son is like a thief who admitted to one partner, and still he pays the fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the father dies, the son becomes one of the heirs, so he owns part of the fine himself. He cannot pay himself, so it is as if one 'partner' dropped out. That leaves only half-shares for the other heirs, yet the משנה says he pays. This seems to show that 'half-oxen' do count, against רב נחמן.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged him (from an accepted source like a משנה)
The four- or fivefold payment
Like one who first admitted
And yet it teaches

phrases.english: He challenged him: If one stole from his father's property,

phrases.english: and slaughtered or sold it, and afterward his father died,
he pays the four- or fivefold payment.
But here, since his father died,

phrases.aramaic: כְּמוֹ שֶׁקָּדַם וְהוֹדָה לְאֶחָד מֵהֶן דָּמֵי,
phrases.english: it is like one who first admitted to one of them,
phrases.notes: The son inherits a share, so his own share of the fine drops away, just like the partner he admitted to.

phrases.english: and yet it teaches: he pays the four- or fivefold payment!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב נחמן's answer in Step 14 using the משנה quoted in Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that 'five half-oxen' do not bring the fine.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the משנה, the son's own inherited share of the fine falls away, leaving only half-shares, yet he still pays the fine. So half-oxen should also bring the fine.

steps.title: The father already took his son to court
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that the משנה is talking about a case where the father brought the son to court before he died, so the full fine was already owed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: What case are we dealing with here? A case where his father stood in court against him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן defends his ruling. He explains that the משנה is about a case where the father sued the son in court while he was still alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the father took the son to court and the son was found guilty, the full fine of whole oxen was already owed to the father. After that, the father's death and the son's inheritance cannot take away the fine. So the משנה is not a case of 'half-oxen', and רב נחמן's ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (introduces a narrower reading of a source)
Stood in court, meaning the case was brought before judges

steps.whatToRemember: At this stage, רב נחמן holds that the Torah's fine requires whole oxen, so admitting to one of two partners exempts the thief from the whole fine. He explains the משנה about the father as a case where the fine was already fixed in court while the father was alive. He takes back this view the next morning in step 19.

phrases.english: He said to him: With what are we dealing here?
Such as where his father stood in court.
phrases.notes: The father brought the son to court before dying, so the full fine was already owed to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge in Step 15 by limiting the case of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case of the משנה (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to be any case where the father died before the trial, so the son's inheritance would leave only half-shares, and still he pays.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is a case where the father already took the son to court while alive, so the full fine of whole oxen was fixed before the father died.

steps.title: רבא asks why the משנה did not split the case itself
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues that if the son is fined only when he stood trial, the משנה should have taught 'if he did not stand trial, he does not pay' instead of bringing a different case in the סיפא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if the son did not stand trial while his father was alive, what would the law be? Would he not pay the four-and-five fine? If so, instead of teaching in the next line, 'He stole from his father, the father died, and afterward he slaughtered or sold it, he does not pay four and five,' the משנה should have split the same case: 'When is this said? When he stood trial. But if he did not stand trial, he does not pay four and five!'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רב נחמן's answer from step 16. He points out that the משנה could have taught the 'no trial' case, but it chose a different example instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן said the son pays only because the father already took him to court. If that were true, the simplest way for the משנה to show when the son is exempt would be to split the very same case into 'stood trial' and 'did not stand trial.' Since the משנה switches to a new case (the father died before the slaughter), it suggests the son pays even without a trial. That would mean partial ownership does not cancel the fine.

keyTerms.meaning: stood trial; was brought to court
the fourfold or fivefold fine for slaughtering or selling a stolen sheep or ox
the latter clause of a משנה
let it make the distinction within that same case
in what case is this said?

phrases.english: But if he did not stand trial, what is the law?
Does he not pay the fourfold and fivefold payment?
If so, instead of teaching the latter clause:
He stole from his father's animals, and the father died,
and afterward he slaughtered or sold it,
he does not pay the fourfold and fivefold payment;
let it make the distinction within that same case:
When is this said? When he stood trial,
but if he did not stand trial,
he does not pay the fourfold and fivefold payment!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's answer in step 16 that the משנה is about a son who already stood trial.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's claim that the משנה is talking only about a case where the son stood trial during the father's lifetime.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If standing trial were the key factor, the משנה should have shown the exemption by splitting the same case, not by switching to a different case. Its choice suggests the son pays even without a trial.

steps.title: רב נחמן explains the משנה's parallel wording
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן agrees that the משנה could have split the case. He says it chose a parallel form so that the סיפא would match the רישא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Yes, it could have. But since the first clause taught 'He stole from his father, slaughtered or sold, and afterward his father died,' the latter clause also used a matching case: 'He stole from his father, his father died, and afterward he slaughtered or sold.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן defends his answer. He admits the משנה could have taught it the other way, but explains that it chose matching wording for style.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן does not deny רבא's point about what the משנה could have said. He explains that the משנה's choice of case comes from wanting the second line to mirror the first line. So nothing can be proven from the fact that the משנה did not split the case.

keyTerms.meaning: indeed so; that is true
since it cited; because it already taught
the first clause of a משנה

phrases.english: He said to him: Indeed, so it could have taught;
since it cited the first clause:
He stole from his father's animals, and slaughtered or sold it,
and afterward his father died;
it cited the latter clause also, in matching form:
He stole from his father's animals, and his father died,
and afterward he slaughtered or sold it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָכִי נָמֵי; אַיְּידֵי דְּנָסֵיב רֵישָׁא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Stylistic explanation: the משנה's wording follows a parallel structure, so its choice of case proves nothing.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא thought the משנה's choice of case shows that the son pays even without a trial.
steps.terutzMaskana: The סיפא was written to mirror the רישא. It does not reveal what happens when the son did not stand trial.
steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן is not admitting he was wrong here. 'הכי נמי' only means 'true, the משנה could have said that.' He still holds his position until the next morning.

steps.title: In the morning, רב נחמן retracts: even five half-oxen count
steps.stepSummary: The next morning, רב נחמן changes his ruling: the Torah's 'five oxen' includes 'five half-oxen.' He then begins to explain why he did not say this the night before.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the morning he said to him: The Torah said 'five oxen,' and that includes even five half-oxen. And the reason I did not tell you this last night...
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן takes back his answer from step 14 and rules that a thief pays the fine even for a partly owned animal. The last line sets up his explanation for why he answered differently the night before; that explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 14, רב נחמן had said 'five oxen, not five half-oxen,' which exempted the thief toward the second partner. Now he reverses himself: a half-share in an ox still counts. So the thief who confessed to one partner still owes the fine to the other partner. This also fits רבא's reading of the משנה about the son.

keyTerms.meaning: in the morning
the Merciful One, meaning the Torah
half-oxen; shares in an ox owned by partners
in the evening; last night

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן's final view: 'five oxen' includes 'five half-oxen.' A thief owes the four-and-five fine even when he only owes it for a share of the animal.
steps.whyThisMatters: This reverses the earlier ruling in step 14. A partial owner's share is enough to trigger the full four-and-five fine on that share.

phrases.english: In the morning he said to him:
"Five oxen," said the Merciful One,
and this includes even five half-oxen.
And the reason that I did not tell you this last night...

steps.triggerLanguage: לְצַפְרָא אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חֲמִשָּׁה בָּקָר אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reverses רב נחמן's original answer in step 14, after the challenges in steps 15 and 17.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: 'Five oxen' includes five half-oxen, so a thief who stole from partners and confessed to one still owes the four-and-five fine to the other.
